chunks: I said to Abu Abdullah (to him), 'The people of Makkah complete the prayer at 'Arafat.' He said, 'Woe to them' or 'Woe be upon them! And which journey is more difficult than it? No, they do not complete (the prayer).'

key_terms.وَيْلَهُمْ: Woe to them (an expression of rebuke)
key_terms.يُتِمُّونَ: They complete (prayer, i.e., pray four rak'ahs instead of two)

ai.seo_question: Do people of Makkah shorten or complete their prayers during Hajj at 'Arafat?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the people of Makkah for completing their prayers at 'Arafat, emphasizing that the state of travel persists there, thus requiring the shortening (Qasr) of the four-rak'ah prayers to two. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the duration and nature of travel, rather than mere location, dictate the obligation of Qasr, distinguishing it from the practice of the Ahl al-Sunnah who often complete prayers at the station of 'Arafat.

en.hubeali: ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The people of Makkah are completing their Salaat at Arafaat’. So heasws said: ‘Woe be unto them’, or said: ‘Woe be upon them! And which journey is more difficult that it? No! Do not (Pray) complete’.
en.sarwar: 5. Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar has narrated the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that people of Makkah perform their Salat (prayer) in complete form when they are in ‘Arafat. He (the Imam) said, ‘Woe is upon them’ or ‘Fie upon them, which journey is more intense than that. No, Salat (prayer) is not complete in ‘Arafat.’”
